blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a swelling in the aorta, the artery that carries blood from the heart to the tummy (abdomen).
Most aneurysms do not cause any problems, but they can be serious because there's a risk they could burst (rupture).

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Symptoms of abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Abdominal aortic aneurysm often has no symptoms.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Symptoms of abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: You usually only find out you have one during an abdominal aortic aneurysm screening test or during tests for another condition.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Symptoms of abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: If an aneurysm gets bigger, you might sometimes notice:

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Symptoms of abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: tummy or back pain

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Symptoms of abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: a pulsing feeling in your tummy

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have tummy or back pain that does not go away or keeps coming back

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you feel a lump in your tummy

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: These symptoms can be caused by lots of things and do not mean you have an abdominal aortic aneurysm, but it's best to get them checked.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Immediate action required: Call 999 if you or someone else:
s: have sudden, severe pain in your tummy or back

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Immediate action required: Call 999 if you or someone else:
s: are struggling to breathe or have stopped breathing

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Immediate action required: Call 999 if you or someone else:
s: have pale or grey skin (on brown or black skin this may be easier to see on the palms of the hands or soles of the feet)

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Immediate action required: Call 999 if you or someone else:
s: lose consciousness

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Immediate action required: Call 999 if you or someone else:
s: These could be signs of an abdominal aortic aneurysm bursting (rupturing).
This is a life-threatening emergency that needs to be treated in hospital as soon as possible.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: The main test to find out if you have an abdominal aortic aneurysm is an ultrasound scan of your tummy.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: A small device is placed on your tummy and images of the inside of your tummy will be shown on a screen.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: You'll usually be told if you have an aneurysm at the end of the test.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: You’ll also be told how big it is:

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: small (3cm to 4.4cm or smaller)

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: medium (4.5cm to 5.4cm)

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: large (5.5cm or bigger)

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm > Screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: An ultrasound test is offered to all men when they turn 65, as they're most at risk of getting an abdominal aortic aneurysm.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Tests for abdominal aortic aneurysm > Screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: This is called abdominal aortic aneurysm screening.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Treatment for an abdominal aortic aneurysm usually depends on how big it is and if you have symptoms.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: If it's small, lifestyle changes such as quitting smoking and eating healthily may be recommended to help stop it getting bigger.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Sometimes you may need:

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: medicines to lower your blood pressure and cholesterol level, which may help stop the aneurysm getting bigger

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: surgery to reduce the risk of the aneurysm bursting - this may be done if your AAA is large (5.5cm or bigger), is quickly getting bigger or is painful

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Surgery has risks and side effects which your doctor or surgeon should discuss with you.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Abdominal aortic aneurysms often get bigger over time.
You'll usually need regular scans to see if it's getting bigger.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Treatment for abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: If your aneurysm ruptures, you’ll need emergency surgery to treat it.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > How to lower your risk of getting an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Making healthy lifestyle changes can help lower your risk of getting an abdominal aortic aneurysm, or stop one from getting bigger.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > How to lower your risk of getting an abdominal aortic aneurysm > Do eat healthily exercise regularly try to lose weight if you're overweight try to cut down on alcohol Don’t
s: do not smoke

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > How to lower your risk of getting an abdominal aortic aneurysm > Do eat healthily exercise regularly try to lose weight if you're overweight try to cut down on alcohol Don’t
s: Find out how to get help to quit smoking

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: An abdominal aortic aneurysm happens when the main artery that carries blood from the heart to the tummy (the aorta) becomes weakened.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: It's not always clear what causes it, but some people have a higher chance of getting one.

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: You’re more at risk if you:

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: are male and aged 65 or over

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: smoke or used to smoke

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: have high blood pressure

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: have high cholesterol

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: have a close relative who's had an abdominal aortic aneurysm

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: have coronary or peripheral artery disease (atherosclerosis)

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: have a condition such as Marfan syndrome

blocks.path: Abdominal aortic aneurysm > Causes of an abdominal aortic aneurysm
s: Sometimes an abdominal aortic aneurysm can be caused by an infection, but this is rare.
